...Readers always love a good bit of artist gossip. Of course, if we kept it up, our magazine would probably get shut down. So to lay low for a while, this issue, we turn our spotlight to another shining star who helped shape the brilliance of Astropolis.

...

Since leaving the Intelligentsia Guild, Ms. Yabuli has never again appeared before the public in person, yet her brilliance, the Life Sciences Institute she founded, and her countless research achievements continue to earn her the admiration of Astropolis's residents.


A Tireless Builder of Astropolis
Where does Ms. Yabuli's day begin? A lab sleep pod, her office desk, or a ship cabin somewhere partway? Any of the above, really, just never her own bed at home.
— Mid-level Researcher ███████

According to the IPC executive who handled outreach and interviewed Yabuli, her résumé wasn't off-the-charts brilliant, but it left a remarkably strong impression nonetheless.

Ever since her student days, this biology enthusiast has been independently researching "physiological acceleration mechanisms related to ether signal transduction." Using herself as the test subject, she refined the technique to a fully applicable level, and by the age of fifteen, had already accumulated twenty-five years' worth of work experience.

Navigating Science and Human Nature
Bacteria are raging, yet a new drug approval takes six whole years? No problem, just turn it into an energy drink and start production. As it turns out, it does not earn any less than the pharmaceutical industry.
— Ms. Yabuli, following her commendation for the mold outbreak incident

...On another note, Ms. Yabuli had visited ██████ in the aftermath of the disaster to provide trade support for local reconstruction efforts. Unfortunately, most of the residents were still deep in grief over the loss of their loved ones and were unable to carry on with their work as usual.

Witnessing the civilization's descent into ruin, Ms. Yabuli acted without hesitation, immediately launching a local "Sample Cloning" initiative. She traced the collective consciousness of the entire world, extracted the "impressions" of the vast majority of lives lost in the disaster, loaded them into brand-new bodies, and then ████████████████████ ██████████████████████.

In the aftermath, she billed the local government entities purely at cost, and leveraging the mutual trust built between them, secured a long term trade contract. This established a firm groundwork for the Technology Department's future resource deployment across the star system.

Over the following decade and more, letters arrived at the Technology Department one after another, expressing deep gratitude toward Ms. Yabuli for helping them reunite with their departed loved ones and friends...

Knowledge Ought to Be Cultivated from Childhood
...A life scholar's heartfelt advice for the future, and a conviction she holds dear.
— Chief Assistant Mastaka

Guided by the Technology Department's forward-looking vision, once the Life Sciences Institute was relocated from Convergence-ξ to Astropolis, her very first directive was to expand its entrance into an ecological garden for visitors of all ages. She went on to reach out to local research institutions across Astropolis, including several classified institutes, to host joint exhibits. This sparked an unprecedented wave of scientific enthusiasm across a youth culture that had been steeped in entertainment for nearly ten centuries.

Ever since, whenever a batch of research results emerged, she made sure to build a showcase model and display it in the ecological park. Wispae, intelligent racing cars... these sights gradually became a natural part of Astropolis. They gave countless children a dream to hold onto, while the admission fees solved the persistent challenge of raising self-directed research funds that had long troubled the institute.

...

Worth noting is that our editorial department has secured an exclusive interview with Ms. Yabuli. Unfortunately, she's currently in the middle of preparing for an important experiment, so it'll have to be pushed back until after March.

Under Ms. Yabuli's guidance, it is eagerly anticipated that Astropolis will elevate its understanding of science to a whole new level.

Astropolis Life, Issue No. 10000410
Editor-in-Chief: MTK
